entities.name: Yang Feng
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Yang Feng emerged as a formidable bandit leader and later a military general during the tumultuous final decades of the Eastern Han dynasty, a period marked by the collapse of central imperial authority and the brutal rise of regional warlords. Active primarily from the early 190s CE until his death in 197, Yang Feng's career intersected with the desperate struggles of Emperor Xian and played a pivotal, albeit transient, role in the power dynamics of the Central Plains, notably in the immediate aftermath of Dong Zhuo's tyranny and the subsequent infighting among his former subordinates, Li Jue and Guo Si. His actions, driven by a blend of self-preservation and opportunistic ambition, briefly positioned him as a protector of the Han emperor, a role that underscored the fragmentation of state power.

Initially leading a substantial force of White Wave Bandits (Baibo Army) in Shanxi, Yang Feng gained prominence by harassing the Han imperial court's remnants following Dong Zhuo's assassination in 192 CE. After the regents Li Jue and Guo Si fell into internecine conflict, Yang Feng, alongside figures like Dong Cheng, played a crucial part in orchestrating Emperor Xian's perilous escape from Chang'an in 195 CE. He briefly sheltered the emperor in Ru City (modern Ruzhou, Henan) and attempted to escort him back to the traditional capital of Luoyang. His forces engaged in numerous skirmishes with Li Jue and Guo Si's pursuing armies, notably at Hongnong and Dongjian, demonstrating both his military capability and the strategic importance of controlling the emperor's person.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Yang Feng's actions as a protector of Emperor Xian in 195-196 CE directly contributed to the circumstances that allowed Cao Cao to gain control of the emperor, a pivotal event that legitimized Cao Cao's subsequent rise to power and reshaped the political landscape of northern China. His defeat and elimination as an independent warlord helped consolidate power for one of the primary architects of the Three Kingdoms period.
